# Control ids CI requires to run, read by ci.yml through required-controls.awk.
#
# One id per line, then each platform whose suite run must run it: ubuntu,
# macos, windows. macos holds both macOS jobs, macos-latest and the bash 3.2
# job, which run on the same image. The suite fails an id listed here that did
# not run on that platform, and says nothing about an id missing from here, so
# CI also fails an id the suite records with ran that is on no line (unless
# ci.yml's NOT_REQUIRED names it) and an id main requires that a change drops
# (unless ci.yml's RETIRED names it).
#
# Name a platform only where the control can run there. A control that
# legitimately skips on a platform fails that job for the wrong reason. Keep
# the lines in byte order (LC_ALL=C sort), so two changes that add ids rarely
# touch the same line. That is a convention, not checked: the reader takes the
# lines in any order.
#
# This file belongs to the template repository. It is excluded from the
# template manifest, and ci.yml drops these requirements outside it.
#
# Why some ids are off a platform, moved here from ci.yml with the lists
# themselves (Release C). "The macOS lists" and "all four" are the two
# macOS jobs and every job, which this file's macos covers as one.
#
# Three lists, not two, because the controls added with the fence,
# retention and hook-cost changes do not all reach every platform.
# Windows reads a backslash in a name as a folder separator, so the
# two that need such a name skip there, only this ubuntu job has
# strace for the process budget, and only its filesystem keeps two
# names that differ in case apart, which promo-create-only-twinguards
# needs. pi-extension-symlink needs a file symlink, which Windows lets
# only a privileged or developer-mode user make; GitHub's Windows
# runners can, so it is required on every job, while a developer's
# machine without the privilege skips it. pi-extension-dirlink uses
# junctions on Windows. retention-unlistable is left off Windows
# because the job's account can list a folder whose listing is denied
# to it, so the case skips there, and retention-posix-mode is left off
# both macOS lists because their bash is 3.2, which cannot parse the
# runner in POSIX mode. mem-override-sink-unreadable and
# mem-override-sink-filelink are left off Windows for the same kind of
# reason: chmod 000 does not stop a listing there, and Git Bash's
# ln -s makes a file link only with a privilege and MSYS=winsymlinks
# set, copying the file otherwise. mem-override-file-mode is left off
# it too, because Git Bash's mode bits are not Windows permissions, and
# so are mem-override-winbin and mem-override-winbin-unreadable (which
# skips under root), because there a claude.exe is the binary
# the runner should start, and mem-override-stray-cygpath and
# mem-override-no-cygpath, because there cygpath is the real one.
# mem-override-mixed-release runs everywhere.
# mem-override-path-refused runs everywhere: on Windows Git Bash keeps
# a double quote or a tab in a name as U+F022 or U+F009 and the pass,
# started as dream-pass.cmd starts it, runs; elsewhere it refuses.
# mem-override-utf8-refused is left off
# Windows, where Git Bash reads a lone byte 0xFF as U+00FF; where the
# file system refuses such a name, as macOS's does, it calls
# memory_override directly. mem-override-utf8-lax-host is recorded
# only where iconv -t UTF-8 lets a sequence above U+10FFFF through, as
# glibc's does, so it is on the ubuntu list only, where it shows that
# job's twins can tell the round trip from a check to UTF-8 alone.
# mem-override-utf16-lax-host is recorded only where iconv -t UTF-16LE
# takes that sequence without an error under LC_ALL=C, the runners'
# locale, as macOS's does, so it is on
# the two macOS lists only, where it shows those twins can tell the
# round trip from a check to UTF-16LE alone. mem-override-unc-refused
# runs everywhere: a cygpath stand-in gives a network path.
# mem-override-work-refused runs everywhere too: a pass with TMPDIR
# inside the vault refuses where mktemp takes TMPDIR, and
# memory_override, called with a folder there, refuses on every
# platform, macOS's among them. mem-override-work-open is off Windows,
# where Git Bash mode bits are not permissions, and so are 1.5.0's
# rf-mode, rf-world, rf-owner and rf-findfail (the runner's own
# folder: its mode, its owner, and a find that cannot check it);
# rf-gone is off Windows too, where the drive path's map-back
# refuses a folder that is not there first;
# rf-owner needs sudo -n, which the hosted runners give. mem-override-work-case
# runs where the file system ignores case, Windows and macOS, so it is
# off the ubuntu list. mem-override-work-root runs everywhere: a
# vault at the root of the temporary folder's file system or drive.
# mem-override-work-resolved runs where mktemp
# takes TMPDIR, so it is off the two macOS lists, and
# mem-override-work-made, a missing folder spelled through a
# link, which must be refused and not made, and a folder for the
# pass that is a link itself, which must be refused, runs wherever
# a link can be made, so it is on all four.
# mem-override-no-iconv
# runs everywhere: a failing iconv stand-in comes first on PATH, and,
# off Windows, a pass also runs with a PATH that holds no iconv.
# mem-override-sink-link uses
# junctions on Windows and runs everywhere.
# mem-override-cygpath-refused needs cygpath, so it is on the Windows
# list only. mem-override-work-colon, mem-override-work-gone,
# mem-override-work-names and mem-override-settings-space run
# everywhere: each calls the library directly, with folders the twin
# makes itself (work-names' two legs with a line break in a folder
# name off Windows only, an INFO line there).
# mem-override-work-root-drive is on the Windows list
# only, because the drive-path walk it holds runs only there.
# mem-override-work-dotdot, mem-override-state-copy and
# mem-override-walk-status run everywhere: each calls the library
# directly (the first through a junction on Windows); work-dotdot's
# dream-pass leg runs where mktemp takes TMPDIR and prints an INFO
# line on macOS. mem-override-work-space is a whole pass with a
# TMPDIR holding a space, so it is off the two macOS lists, whose
# mktemp ignores TMPDIR. mem-override-work-backstop runs everywhere,
# its legs with a folder name ending in a line break and its
# dangling-link legs off Windows only (an INFO line there).
# mem-override-work-unreachable (a folder this
# account cannot enter) and mem-override-vault-unresolved (a vault
# that is not there, which cygpath's round trip refuses first on
# Windows) are off the Windows list: Git Bash's mode bits are not
# Windows permissions, and there an account may by default pass
# through a folder it cannot enter. temp-dir-spelling runs
# everywhere: its runner legs hand each runner the spelling through
# a mktemp stand-in, so macOS's mktemp does not matter, and off
# Windows a cygpath stand-in makes the platform read as Windows; its
# leg where the check must do nothing runs off Windows only, with no
# cygpath on PATH.
